title: Linear form in $\log 2, \log 3, \log c$: explicit Baker–Wüstholz lower bound
author: @alon yuval
source: Implied by Matveev, Izv. Math. 64 (2000) 1217-1269 (restated as Bugeaud-Mignotte-Siksek, Ann. Math. 163 (2006), Thm 9.4). Verified against two independent open-access restatements that agree verbatim: arXiv:1905.01015 Thm 2.3 and arXiv:2207.12860 (Ddamulira-Luca) Thm 2.2: for positive real γ_i in a real field of degree D, Γ = ∏γ_i^{b_i} - 1 ≠ 0 ⇒ log|Γ| > -1.4·30^{t+3}·t^{4.5}·D²(1+log D)(1+log B)A_1⋯A_t, A_i ≥ max(D h(γ_i), |log γ_i|, 0.16). Here t=3, D=1, γ=(2,3,c), b=(k-1,-i,1), B ≤ 2i+1, A=(log 2, log 3, max(log c,0.16) ≤ log 4i): constant ≈ 9.9e10 vs 2^42 ≈ 4.4e12, margin ≈ 43x (checked for i=2^60..2^200); passing from Γ to Λ = log(Γ+1) costs at most log 2. Also implied by Baker-Wüstholz, J. reine angew. Math. 442 (1993) 19-62 (constant 2^42 as in rwst/bbchallenge, CC0).

author: @Secousses
source: Special case of: Y. O. Hamidoune, A note on minimal directed graphs with given girth, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 43 (1987), no. 3, 343–348, which proves the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture for minimum out-degree r = 3 (every loopless digraph on n vertices with minimum out-degree 3 has a directed cycle of length at most ⌈n/3⌉). Here the conclusion is restricted to digraphs having a nonempty set S with 1 ≤ |∂⁺S| ≤ 2 and S ∪ ∂⁺S ≠ V. Conjecture: L. Caccetta and R. Häggkvist, On minimal digraphs with given girth, Congr. Numer. 21 (1978), 181–187. Origin of this statement: it is the remaining case of a reduction of TenChallenges.challenge_03_r3 (Caccetta–Häggkvist, r = 3). That reduction uses strong induction on n, a ball-growth argument when every out-boundary that does not cover the digraph has at least 3 vertices, and the induction hypothesis on the subdigraph induced by a nonempty set with empty out-boundary.
